failure_modes.name: Insufficient_Retrieved_Evidence
failure_modes.evidence: Summary_1 explicitly names missing evidence: 'To complete verification, evidence documents would be needed regarding: (1) which NFL team, if any, plays or played their home games at Ebbets Field'. Summary_2 names missing evidence: 'To verify this claim, passages would be needed that: (1) identify who Jason Pinkston is and document his family connections, (2) name a specific footballer related to Jason Pinkston, and (3) confirm that this footballer played his entire career with the Brooklyn Dodgers (NFL) at Ebbets Field.' The hop 3 query explicitly targets the missing evidence: 'Did the Brooklyn Dodgers NFL team play their home games at Ebbets Field, and if so, during what years? What is the complete roster or player history of the Brooklyn Dodgers (NFL)?' However, the retrieved passages confirm the Brooklyn Dodgers (NFL) played at Ebbets Field but provide no roster information or any player who played their entire career there and is related to Jason Pinkston - a corpus gap.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Passage_Content_Misreading
failure_modes.evidence: Summary_1 states: 'Based on historical fact (outside the passages), no NFL team has ever played at Ebbets Field, which was a baseball stadium, making the foundational premise of the claim impossible to satisfy.' This contradicts hop 1 passage [4] about David Diehl and directly contradicts the Ebbets Field passage in hop 3 which explicitly states Ebbets Field 'was also home to three National Football League teams in the 1920s.' The solver misread or failed to process that NFL teams did play at Ebbets Field.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 1 summary devotes extensive reasoning to passages [3-7] about Bill Stevenson (CFL), David Diehl (Giants), Mo Collins (Raiders), Jim Yarbrough (Lions), and Keith Dorney (Lions) - none of whom are related to Jason Pinkston, played for teams at Ebbets Field, or are relevant to the claim. The summary does not explain why these passages were retrieved or analyzed when passages [1] and [2] already established the cousin relationship and team affiliations.
